column1: # assay_types.tsv — controlled vocabulary for tolerance-measurement `assay_type` (PLAN.md I.3:
# "Every tolerance measurement carries assay_type ... and the atlas will not aggregate across
# assay types silently").
# THIS FILE IS LOAD-BEARING: "tolerance" is not one phenotype and these assay types are NOT
# interconvertible with each other. A growth-rate-at-x-percent result and an IC50 both describe
# "ethanol tolerance" in English, but they are different measurements of different quantities —
# one is a rate observed at one fixed concentration, the other is a concentration at which a
# response reaches 50%. Silently averaging or equating them across assay_type is exactly the
# error PLAN.md I.3 exists to prevent. Every row below repeats this in its own `note` column
# rather than relying on a single shared sentence, because a query that filters this table is
# likely to see one row at a time.
# Columns:
#   assay_type            the closed vocabulary value
#   description             what is measured and how
#   output_measure          the quantity actually reported (with its natural unit family)
#   comparable_across_concentration   whether a single run of this assay type sweeps
#                          concentration (yes) or is read at one fixed, separately-recorded
#                          condition (no) — relevant to how it can be plotted, not a license to
#                          convert it to another assay_type
#   note                   explicit non-interconvertibility statement plus assay-specific caveat
#   evidence, confidence
# Evidence-honesty pass (this revision, following the compartments.tsv D1 rewrite): every row
# below that was 'high' solely on the strength of citing another fermdb file (PLAN.md,
# docs/reference/CONVENTIONS.md, a source module, or another vocabulary TSV) has been changed to
# 'unverified' -- citing an internal document is citing memory with an extra hop, not an
# independent check. A row stays 'high' only when its evidence names something actually checked
# outside the repo in this session (e.g. a ChEBI lookup via web search). The confidence vocabulary
# is closed and has four values everywhere ('unverified', 'low', 'medium', 'high'; D2);
# 'unverified' means asserted but never checked against a source, distinct from 'low' (checked,
# weak).
assay_type
growth_rate_in_x_percent
column2: Specific growth rate (mu) measured in culture held at one fixed, named stressor concentration.
column3: specific growth rate (1/h) at a stated concentration
column4: no — one concentration per measurement row; a dose-response curve is a set of these rows, not a single assay
column5: NOT interconvertible with viability_after_shock, IC50, MIC, lag_extension, spot_dilution or adapted_growth: this is a continuous-culture rate under chronic exposure, not a survival fraction, a half-maximal concentration, a binary growth/no-growth call, a lag time, or an evolved endpoint.
column6: PLAN.md I.3 ("growth rate in x%") and B.5 point 4 (no silent aggregation across assay types)

column1: viability_after_shock
column2: Fraction of cells that survive a single, typically brief, exposure to a stressor (e.g. plating efficiency or live/dead stain after a shock), as distinct from growth under chronic exposure.
column4: no — one exposure condition (concentration x duration) per measurement row
column5: NOT interconvertible with growth_rate_in_x_percent, IC50, MIC, lag_extension, spot_dilution or adapted_growth: this is a survival fraction after an acute shock, not a chronic growth rate, a dose-response parameter, a lag time, or an evolved endpoint.
column6: PLAN.md I.3 ("viability after shock") and B.5 point 4

column1: IC50
column2: The stressor concentration at which a chosen response (commonly growth or viability) is reduced to 50% of its unstressed value, fit from a dose-response curve.
column3: concentration at half-maximal inhibition (same unit as the stressor, e.g. g/L or % v/v)
column4: yes — this assay_type IS the summary of a concentration sweep, but the sweep's raw points are a different measurement (growth_rate_in_x_percent or viability_after_shock) feeding into this fit
column5: NOT interconvertible with MIC even though both are single-number dose-response summaries: IC50 is a continuous half-maximal-response concentration from a fitted curve, MIC is a binary no-visible-growth threshold read directly off a dilution series, and the two use different response definitions and typically differ numerically for the same organism/stressor pair. Also not interconvertible with growth_rate_in_x_percent, viability_after_shock, lag_extension, spot_dilution or adapted_growth.
column6: PLAN.md I.3 groups "IC50/MIC" together as one bullet, but B.5 point 4's rule against silent cross-assay-type aggregation is read here as applying to IC50 vs MIC as well, since they are fit from different response definitions (unverified: this split of PLAN.md's combined "IC50/MIC" bullet into two rows is this curator's judgement call, flagged for a curator to confirm or merge)

column1: MIC
column2: Minimum Inhibitory Concentration: the lowest tested concentration at which no visible growth is observed, read directly off a dilution series (a threshold, not a curve fit).
column3: concentration (same unit as the stressor); censored by the tested dilution series' spacing
column4: yes — read from a concentration series, but reported as one threshold value, not a curve
column5: NOT interconvertible with IC50 (see IC50 row for why), nor with growth_rate_in_x_percent, viability_after_shock, lag_extension, spot_dilution or adapted_growth. An MIC value is also right-censored by the dilution series tested and should carry is_upper_bound / detection_limit style flags rather than being treated as an exact point estimate (by analogy with PLAN.md C.6's is_below_lod / is_upper_bound fields on `measurement`).

column1: lag_extension
column2: How much longer the lag phase becomes under a stressor, relative to an unstressed control — a delay-to-growth measure, not a rate or survival measure.
column3: extension of lag time (h), typically stressed-lag minus control-lag
column4: no — one stressor condition (vs. its own control) per measurement row
column5: NOT interconvertible with growth_rate_in_x_percent, viability_after_shock, IC50, MIC, spot_dilution or adapted_growth: a strain can show a long lag but a normal post-lag growth rate, or vice versa, so lag extension and growth rate are genuinely independent axes of "tolerance" and must never be averaged together or substituted for one another.
column6: PLAN.md I.3 ("lag extension") and B.5 point 4

column1: spot_dilution
column2: Qualitative-to-semiquantitative growth readout from a serial-dilution spot assay on solid media, typically scored by number of visible dilution spots or a categorical growth score relative to a control.
column3: ordinal/categorical growth score (assay-specific scale; record the scale used) or highest dilution showing visible growth
column4: no — one plate (stressor condition) per measurement row, itself a small dilution series
column5: NOT interconvertible with the liquid-culture assay types above (growth_rate_in_x_percent, viability_after_shock, IC50, MIC, lag_extension) or with adapted_growth: this is a solid-media, typically ordinal readout, not a continuous rate, concentration or time, and its resolution is limited by the dilution steps used, which differ between papers.
column6: PLAN.md I.3 ("spot dilution") and B.5 point 4

column1: adapted_growth
column2: Growth outcome after a period of laboratory adaptation/evolution under the stressor, describing an evolved endpoint rather than the naive (unadapted) strain's response.
column3: whichever quantity was reported for the evolved endpoint (e.g. an evolved growth rate or an evolved MIC) — record which, via a separate quantity_kind/basis, not by conflating it with the naive-strain value
column4: no — describes a strain history (naive vs. adapted), not a single concentration sweep
column5: NOT interconvertible with the naive-strain assay types above: an adapted_growth result reflects a genetically or physiologically changed population (see PLAN.md I.4's adaptive_evolution modification type) and must never be pooled with a naive-strain growth_rate_in_x_percent, viability_after_shock, IC50, MIC, lag_extension or spot_dilution result as if it were the same measurement on the same organism.
column6: Named explicitly in this file's own task brief as a required assay_type; PLAN.md I.3's assay_type list does not name it directly but PLAN.md I.4 lists adaptive_evolution as a modification type whose measured_effect would use this assay_type (unverified: this cross-reference is this curator's inference, not a quoted PLAN.md line)

column1: competitive_growth
column2: Relative fitness of two or more strains grown together in the same vessel under a stressor, read out as a change in relative abundance rather than an absolute rate for any one strain.
column3: change in relative abundance / competitive index over time (dimensionless ratio or log-ratio per unit time)
column4: no — one co-culture condition per measurement row
column5: NOT interconvertible with any single-strain assay type above (growth_rate_in_x_percent, viability_after_shock, IC50, MIC, lag_extension, spot_dilution, adapted_growth): a competitive index depends on the specific competitor used and on relative, not absolute, performance, so it answers a different question even when the same stressor and strain are involved.
column6: PLAN.md I.3 lists "competition" alongside viability after shock, IC50/MIC, lag extension and spot dilution as an assay_type; included here under the more specific name competitive_growth
